name: Sion
notes: Roar of the Slayer (E) opens the fight for its 0.25 s cast and its 25% armor shred, then Decimating Smash (Q), Soul Furnace (W) and basic attacks fill the rest of the window on cooldown/readiness; the engine casts Unstoppable Onslaught (R) automatically at t = 0 since it is learned.

Decimating Smash (Q) is held for its full damage ramp before releasing: this is read as 1 second of charge, since the ability's own range/knock-up/stun data table only extends to a 1 s charge time, resolving an unsettled ramp-cap question in favour of the better-documented, shorter reading rather than assuming the ramp continues across the full 2 s charge window.

Unstoppable Onslaught (R) is held for its full 3-second damage ramp before ending in a slam, which lands after the ending leap's 0.55 s travel time; the stationary dummy is assumed not to force an earlier collision, matching the dossier's proposed rotation of holding for maximum damage.

While Decimating Smash charges or Unstoppable Onslaught channels/leaps, Sion's basic attacks and his other non-Soul-Furnace abilities are locked out, per the wiki's channel-interaction tables (only Soul Furnace remains castable throughout either).

Soul Furnace (W) is cast for its shield and recast at the minimum 3 s delay to detonate immediately for magic damage, since nothing damages the shield in this fight and holding it longer adds nothing; its target-max-health damage ratio is read from the numbers sheet's ranked SionW.DamagePercentHealthTooltip array (10% to 14% by rank) rather than the ability text's single flat '14%' figure, since the by-rank sheet data is the more precise source.

Only the initial press of Decimating Smash, Soul Furnace and Unstoppable Onslaught counts as an ability activation for on-cast effects (Spellblade, Muramana, Eclipse); their damage-dealing recast/detonation/slam does not, per the wiki's explicit notes for Soul Furnace and Unstoppable Onslaught, extended here to Decimating Smash for consistency across the champion's three charge-then-release abilities.

Glory in Death (passive) and Death Surge are not modeled: the dummy never damages Sion, so he never dies and the zombie-state effects (attack speed, life steal, on-hit max-health damage) never trigger.
Soul Furnace's shield, and the slows/knock-ups/stuns on Q, E and R, are not modeled since the dummy never attacks and is never displaced; only each ability's damage instance is dealt.
Mana costs are not modeled: nothing here is mana-gated within a short level-16 dummy fight.

assumed.why: Decimating Smash's own range/knock-up/stun data table only lists charge times from 0 to 1 second in 0.25 s steps, so its damage ramp is read as completing at 1 second of hold rather than continuing across the full 2-second charge window; the dossier flags this as an open question and this is the better-supported reading.
